clue.text: Immediately visiting tourist attraction

definitions.meaning: straight away, on first glance, without further thought
taken literally, the moment you are at a sight worth seeing for the first time

explanation.surface: A tourist goes straight off to see the local attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means on first viewing, hence immediately; literally it describes the first look at a sight.

clue.text: A member giving support, very clued-up and relevant

parts.note: a prop is a rugby forward who supports the scrum, or any support

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: A well-informed club member's supportive remarks are very much to the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clued-up' reads as well-informed, but its 'up' turns the word for very upwards in this down entry; a prop is a supporting rugby forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means pertinent or to the point, a synonym of relevant.

clue.text: Oxymoron is possibly too cryptically described

definitions.meaning: a rhetorical device such as 'deafening silence'
said aloud, the word too is the number two, so it is a figure in speech

explanation.surface: Someone thinks calling something an oxymoron is perhaps too clever by half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is possibly' marks the oxymoron as one example. The second reading is a pun: 'too' sounds like the figure 2.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxymoron is one example of a rhetorical device; the pun makes 'too' a spoken numeral.

clue.text: Verse from Frost recital

indicators.note: a recital is something spoken aloud, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: A poem by Robert Frost is read aloud at a recital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' looks like the poet but is the weather word RIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyme can mean verse or poetry in general, as in nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Article in which one's detected actual plagiarism?

indicators.note: in which places the numeral for one inside the article
detected says one is found sitting within the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
I is the Roman numeral one, with 's meaning is
very means actual, as in the very thing

explanation.surface: An article is found to contain genuine plagiarism.
explanation.definitionFit: Plagiarism is the theft of others' words, so it is a kind of stealing; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Someone much loved ruined part of holiday

indicators.note: ruined says the selected letters are wrecked and reassembled
part of means a run of letters is taken from inside the word holiday

explanation.surface: A beloved person spoils part of a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' takes OLID from inside 'holiday'; 'ruined' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a person greatly adored, a hero or favourite.

clue.text: Up and running on this?

parts.note: up in the saddle, with your mount at a gallop beneath you

explanation.surface: A project is up and running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up and running' is a business idiom, but here it means mounted and galloping.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding on an animal's back, you are up high while it runs.

clue.text: Work one poet's composed with less feeling, for colleague elsewhere

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: composed suggests the letters are put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
number means more numb, having less sensation

explanation.surface: A poet writes a piece with emotional detachment, for a colleague abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges I and POETS to give POSITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Your counterpart is the person in the same role in another organisation, a colleague elsewhere.

clue.text: Rush second hot meal?

parts.note: a curry is a spicy dish

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off to a second spicy dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry is to move hurriedly with short quick steps.

clue.text: Handled the ball? Not out in this case

definitions.text: Handled the ball? Not out in this case

parts.words: Handled the ball? Not out in this case
parts.note: in cricket 'handled the ball' was a way of being given out, but in one football code carrying the ball in the hands is the whole point

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire ponders whether a batsman who handled the ball is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handled the ball' is a cricket mode of dismissal, so the surface points at cricket; the clue asks for the game in which handling is legal and nobody is out for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description of the football code played with the hands, where handling never gets a player dismissed.

clue.text: Is nothing right in debatable item — having properties equally distributed?

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for right is placed inside the debatable item

parts.note: a topic is a subject up for debate

explanation.surface: Someone argues over whether a disputed thing has evenly spread qualities.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical synonym: an isotropic material has the same physical properties in every direction.

clue.text: Apprehend peer involved with vice

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters of the two words are entangled and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman is arrested for his part in some immoral activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apprehend' looks like arrest, matching the police surface, but here it means grasp mentally.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprehend in the sense of understand or notice is to perceive something.

clue.text: Read avidly most of the day before, outwardly grim

indicators.note: outwardly means the word for grim sits on the outside, wrapping the other piece

parts.note: dour means stern or grim

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped from the word for the day before

parts.note: eve is the day before a festival, as in Christmas Eve

explanation.surface: A gloomy person reads eagerly most of the evening before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read avidly' is one idea, so 'Read' is not a separate piece; 'most of' and 'outwardly' are the two indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: To devour a book is a common idiom for reading it eagerly and quickly.

clue.text: Promised to hold dance, as something long in store?

indicators.note: to hold means the word for promised contains the dance word

parts.note: sworn means pledged or promised
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Someone has vowed to put on a dance, and asks about an old stock item.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods left long on display in a store become faded and grubby, which is literally what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Pulled out of being shy

definitions.meaning: taken out, as money from a bank or troops from a front

explanation.surface: A timid person backs out of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The past participle of withdraw means pulled out; as an adjective it means retiring or shy.

clue.text: Political group, one going in for equal status

indicators.note: going in means the letter for one is placed inside the political group

parts.note: a party is a political organisation
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A political party admits one new member who demands equal rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is equality of standing, pay or value, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Something soothing in speech for Queen's address?

parts.note: a balm is a soothing ointment
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a soothing phrase for the Queen's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen's address' suggests a royal speech; it is her home. BALMORAL is the royal family's Scottish castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle is a residence of the monarch in Scotland, so it is an address of the Queen.

clue.text: It's a nuisance at first about European currency being superseded

indicators.note: about means the pest goes round the European abbreviation

parts.note: a pest is an annoying person or thing

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word at

explanation.surface: Someone complains that it was a bother to switch from a European currency being replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives A and 'about' puts E inside PEST. The peseta was Spain's currency until the euro replaced it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish peseta was a currency then being phased out in favour of the euro.

clue.text: Quickly take steps to provide conjuror's monologue

definitions.meaning: to run with quick light taps of the feet
the smooth chat a magician uses during a trick

explanation.surface: A magician moves fast to supply his stage talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To patter is to move with light quick steps; patter is also a performer's rapid line of talk.

clue.text: Second tour of duty? One may get into the rhythm -

definitions.text: One may get into the rhythm

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
a beat is a police officer's regular patrol round

explanation.surface: A soldier on a second tour of duty finds his marching rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal number but is the verb meaning to support.
explanation.definitionFit: A backbeat is the accented off-beat in popular music, a rhythm listeners get into.

clue.text: Torn between not getting up, or seeing state capital

indicators.note: between means the word for torn sits in the middle of the other piece
in a down clue, getting up means the word is written upwards

parts.note: taken as written
rent means torn

explanation.surface: Someone torn between staying in bed and visiting a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torn between' looks like indecision, but Torn is the fodder and 'between' the container signal. Trenton is the capital of New Jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenton is the capital city of the US state of New Jersey.

clue.text: —in attempt to secure aim

indicators.note: to secure means the attempt holds the aim inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: someone tries to get a grip on a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash links this clue to 18's; the definition is just 'in', as in fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is in is fashionable, the same as trendy.

clue.text: Ruminate about motorway replacing new green

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged
replacing means the motorway letter takes the place of the letter for new

parts.note: M is the British abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a motorway being built over a village green.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap N for M in RUMINATE to get RUMIMATE, then 'about' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or not yet grown up, so it is a synonym for unripe and childish.

clue.text: A mostly laughably passé form of seeding

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: corny means trite and dated in a laughable way

explanation.surface: A dated, rather silly way of sowing seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the seed of the oak, the form an oak tree takes when it seeds.

clue.text: Prepare artwork in France and Switzerland

parts.note: et is French for and
CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: An artist prepares work in France and Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a design into a plate, preparing it for printing as artwork.

clue.text: One charming song cut? Join in to keep it

indicators.note: to keep means the word for join in holds the shortened song

parts.note: to enter is to join in or take part

indicators.note: cut means the song loses its final letter

parts.note: a chant is a simple song

explanation.surface: A charming singer's song is cut short, and others are invited to join in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One charming' suggests a charming person; it means one who casts spells. 'it' is a link referring back to the cut song.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchanter is someone who casts spells, literally one who charms.

clue.text: Surely it isn't short circuit?

parts.note: the electrical fault is a red herring: read it as a circuit round a planet, which is anything but short

explanation.surface: An electrician wonders whether a fault is a short circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short circuit' suggests electrics; instead the circuit is a long path traced around a star or planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description of a celestial path, a circuit round a body that covers vast distances.

clue.text: Eventually making a marathon effort

definitions.meaning: literally, taking part in a race of great length

explanation.surface: Someone finally succeeds after a long and gruelling effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means ultimately; read literally it describes running a long race such as a marathon.
